newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Airways Corp saves after dropping AA contract.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Airways Corp saves after dropping AA contract.

text.p: The cost of buying out a contract to provide flight inspection of navigation aids will be recovered within a year, New Zealand's Airways Corporation said on Monday.
The state-owned enterprise in April paid an undisclosed sum to terminate a NZ$13 million ten-year contract with state-owned Airservices Australia (AA) when it still had four years to run.
"The buy-out will pay for itself within a year," Airways chief executive Craig Sinclair said in a statement, adding that the cost of flight inspection using the new technology had almost halved.
"Because of the savings we are making using the new technology we are able to pass the benefits on to our customers both in New Zealand and the Pacific", he added.
Airways Corp began operating its own flight inspection service using new compact calibrating equipment that had not been available when the Australian contract began.
The new equipment is carried in a Mitsubishi MU-2 aircraft owned by Auckland-based Air National. This is a smaller aircraft than the Fokker F28 jetliner used for the older equipment.
